elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph warrants only that services "will conform in all material respects to the applicable Research Plan or Development Plan for thirty (30) days following performance"; no professional-and-workmanlike/industry-standard performance standard appears anywhere in Article XIII.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "any software delivered by RevMed to Sanofi under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — the disjunctive element is satisfied by the software-to-documentation warranty.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery," not twelve months.
Services warranty runs only "thirty (30) days following performance."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "RevMed will repair or replace the non-conforming software, re-perform the non-conforming services..."
"...or refund the amounts paid for the non-conforming software or services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts a mutual Applicable Law covenant at Section 13.4(b), but that text is not in the cited or rendered operative language, so compliance-with-laws coverage cannot be verified here; it is in any event not addressed by the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code, virus, or disabling-device warranty appears in the inserted text or elsewhere in the rendered Article XIII.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "(i) any software delivered by RevMed to Sanofi under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to its documentation for ninety (90) days following delivery" — meets the 90-day floor with an express software-to-documentation warranty.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "(ii) the services RevMed performs under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to the applicable Research Plan or Development Plan for thirty (30) days following performance."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "RevMed will repair or replace the non-conforming software, re-perform the non-conforming services" — express repair/replacement remedy.
"or refund the amounts paid for the non-conforming software or services" — express refund remedy.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor, an express 30-day services conformance warranty, and both repair/replacement (plus re-performance) and refund remedies in a single sentence.

Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, services period is 30 days rather than 90, no malicious-code warranty, and compliance with Applicable Law is only asserted (Section 13.4(b)) rather than shown in the rendered text.

Minimality holds: the redline is a pure insertion placed inside Article XIII, deletes nothing, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure, cure period, or extra damages categories, and adds no requirement outside the fallback checklist. Re-performance is a natural variant of the repair/replace remedy for services, not a separate obligation on Vendor beyond the checklist.

Intent is preserved: Section 13.5 carves out anything "EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII," so siting the new warranty in Article XIII keeps it outside the disclaimer without editing 13.5; the existing representations, covenants 13.3(a)-(d) and the mutual disclaimer survive without contradiction.

Drafting nit (not a failure): the inserted paragraph follows the 13.3 lead-in "RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:" but is a free-standing sentence rather than a lettered subsection; number it expressly (e.g., new Section 13.3(e) or a new Section 13.4A) so it plainly reads as an Article XIII warranty and not as an orphan continuation of the covenant list.

Also confirm that "Development Plan" (and "Research Plan") are defined terms in the Agreement; if "Development Plan" is undefined, the services conformance benchmark would rest on an undefined trigger and should be replaced with a defined plan reference or a professional-and-workmanlike standard.
